Q178: There is so much bush honeysuckle, over so many acres, that we're only able to barely make a dent in it with current staff/time/resources.  If resources were not a barrier, I would sign up large acreages for EQIP funding brush management, then contract out these large acreages to be gone over with a Fecon brush cutter followed by herbicide treatment for the less steep areas and have an army of hand-cutters, stump treatment contractors address treat the brush on steep slopes inappropriate for the equipment.  When cost share has been available, we have done this on as many acres as we could obtain funding on (90 acres) but even that is not a lot when we have about 3,000 acres affected by honeysuckle brush.
